This page corresponds to the exact occupation U.S. O*NET/SOC 29-9021.00 "Health Information Technologists and Medical Registrars" (Health Information Technologists and Medical Registrars): apply knowledge of healthcare and information systems to assist in the design, development, and continued modification and analysis of computerized healthcare systems; abstract, collect, and analyze treatment and followup information of patients; may educate staff and assist in problem solving to promote the implementation of the healthcare information system; may design, develop, test, and implement databases with complete history, diagnosis, treatment, and health status to help monitor diseases. Official scope text: Apply knowledge of healthcare and information systems to assist in the design, development, and continued modification and analysis of computerized healthcare systems. Abstract, collect, and analyze treatment and followup information of patients. May educate staff and assist in problem solving to promote the implementation of the healthcare information system. May design, develop, test, and implement databases with complete history, diagnosis, treatment, and health status to help monitor diseases. The core tasks listed by O*NET include: using the relevant computer software to assign patients to diagnosis-related groups (DRG); compiling medical and census data to produce statistical reports on diseases treated, surgeries performed, or bed occupancy; designing databases that support healthcare applications and ensuring security, performance, and reliability; developing in-service education materials; evaluating and recommending upgrades or improvements to existing computerized healthcare systems; promoting and facilitating activities such as brown-bag lunches, workshops, or tours to foster awareness of medical information privacy or security within the organization; using standard classification systems to identify, compile, abstract, and code patient data; managing a department or supervising clerical staff and directing or controlling the activities of medical records department staff; monitoring changes in legislation and accreditation standards that affect the security or privacy of computerized healthcare systems; planning, developing, maintaining, or operating various health record indexes or storage and retrieval systems to collect, classify, store, or analyze information; compiling statistical reports, narrative reports, or graphic presentations (such as tumor registry data) for hospital staff, researchers, or other users; protecting the security of medical records to ensure confidentiality; consulting with physicians or others, or clarifying codes or diagnoses at coding team meetings, regarding conflicting, missing, or ambiguous information; retrieving patient records for physicians, technicians, or other medical personnel; training medical records staff; and writing or maintaining archived processes, procedure codes, or application queries. Common job titles include Medical Records Analyst and Medical Records Director. Scope note: the wage and employment and industry data presented by O*NET on the 29-9021.00 page are not marked as taken from a parent occupation, so this page labels them faithfully according to this occupation's own scope (29-9021.00); the page also shows a projected 2024—2034 growth of "Much faster than average (7% or higher)" (much faster than average) and marks it Bright Outlook (good prospects); it should also be noted that this page is a "subset profile" and does not yet provide work context percentages or task importance scores, so this page marks the corresponding dimensions with "Evidence insufficient:" rather than filling them in. Scope and boundaries are described in the sections below.

Exercise prompt | A completely fictional medical coding and health information system implementation task package (for practice workflow only; it does not represent any real institution, system, patient, or data). Write a draft plan: (1) how, based on a fictional medical record along with clinical coding notes and an information system requirements document, to arrange a structured medical coding and information system support task (identification of users and clinical needs and workflows, data and classification standards and sources, coding and abstraction and validation, privacy and security and access control, registration and indexes and retrieval, statistical reporting and quality monitoring, ethics and compliance and informed boundaries), and state which information is insufficient and needs to be supplemented (medical record completeness and coding basis, classification and terminology standards and mapping, system interfaces and retrieval and performance, privacy and security and minimum necessary requirements, registration and indexes and statistical definitions, quality validation and review and fallback plans); (2) how to design the completion and review points for a fictional coding, registration, and system operation log table (fields and definitions, patients and roles and permissions, codes and abstraction and versions and changes, data entry and validation, exceptions and omissions and handling, review and audit trail); (3) how to write a handover-ready task description (needs and objectives—standards and mapping—coding and validation—privacy and security—registration and retrieval—quality and open items); (4) how to record and preserve medical records and coding, registration, and system data, and distinguish disclosable information from controlled materials or materials involving patient health information and protected health information; (5) how to pause, review, and escalate when a medical record is unclear or the coding basis is insufficient or standards do not match, when a system deviates from compliance requirements, when a security or privacy risk arises, when clinical judgment or medical advice is involved, or when the task exceeds the position's authorization. Answer using public materials and simulated data; do not use any real patient data or personal health information.

Fit signals | The interest code for U.S. O*NET 29-9021.00 is CIS (Conventional—Investigative—Social), with occupational interest type scores of Conventional (83), Investigative (70), and Social (47); the specific interest areas with higher scores are Information Technology (76), Clerical (74), and Health Care Services (57); the work style influence scores that rank highest are Attention to Detail (92), Dependability (88), Integrity (84), Cautiousness (76), and Curiosity (66). These orientations correspond to: a willingness to process medical records, coding, and registration item by item according to standards and specifications (Conventional), a willingness to study and verify classification standards and data and statistics (Investigative), and a willingness to communicate and collaborate with medical personnel, the coding team, and management and user departments (Social), while maintaining a high degree of caution regarding patient information security and data accuracy. If you are willing to process medical records, coding, registration, and retrieval item by item according to standards and specifications, can communicate with clinical and management departments, and are willing to take responsibility for data accuracy and patient information privacy, the daily requirements of this occupation are closer to the way you work. O*NET 29-9021.00 is a "subset profile" and does not provide work context percentages; this page does not fill them in with values from adjacent occupations.

Caution signals | It must be stated faithfully (29-9021.00): this O*NET page is a "subset profile" (data collection is still in progress), and this round it does not provide work context percentages or task importance scores, so this page marks the corresponding dimensions with "Evidence insufficient:" rather than filling them in with values from adjacent occupations. The verifiable orientation signals are the interest code CIS (Conventional 83 / Investigative 70 / Social 47) and the work style influences (Attention to Detail 92, Dependability 88, Integrity 84, Cautiousness 76, Curiosity 66). This occupation deals with medical records, coding, registration, health information systems, and patient information security; a single coding or abstraction error, a single incorrect grouping (DRG) or distortion of statistical definitions, a single loss of control over a medical record version or index record, a single improper access control or handling of patient information, or a single instance of issuing conclusions or disclosing information beyond authorization can all cause distorted clinical and statistical results, damage to patient privacy, and compliance and legal risk. O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Three (medium preparation needed, SVP 6.0 to less than 7.0); the education section of that page does not show a percentage distribution, and this page does not fill it in. The daily work of this occupation requires long hours processing medical records, coding, systems, and data and facing pressure at coding, statistical, and compliance checkpoints, and it generally requires strong attentiveness, adherence to standards, and a sense of confidentiality. If you find it hard to check and record item by item according to standards over the long term, hard to bear responsibility for patient information and data accuracy and the consequences of errors, or unwilling to take responsibility for the truthfulness of the coding basis and privacy compliance, you should treat these as real costs that need careful weighing.

Ownership judgment | Real fit comes from whether you can do three things at once on the same medical record and health information task: do the profession properly (complete coding, abstraction, registration, retrieval, and statistics based on medical records, classification standards, and information system requirements, cite practices consistent with current standards and specifications, and produce usable coding, registration, index, retrieval, and statistical records), keep compliance, privacy, and boundaries under control (work and keep an audit trail in line with patient information privacy, security, informed consent, and data protection requirements; distinguish disclosable information from controlled materials or materials involving patient health information and protected health information and handle them according to policy; and do not overstep by providing clinical judgment or medical diagnosis and medication advice), and take on definable position responsibility (be accountable for the coding, abstraction, registration, system operations, statistics, and records you personally perform, and refer matters beyond authorization or involving clinical judgment, medical advice, or external disclosure to the appropriate position or institution according to policy). It is recommended to test this with one verifiable experience (completing a coding, registration, and retrieval record and a statistical report note for a fictional medical record, or a retrospective review of handling one coding dispute or privacy risk) rather than relying only on the conclusions of an interest questionnaire.

Direct answer | The "Health Information Technologists and Medical Registrars" on this page is the exact occupation O*NET 29-9021.00 (Health Information Technologists and Medical Registrars), and the work can be divided into several categories: first, medical records and coding — using standard classification systems to identify, compile, abstract, and code patient data; using the relevant software to assign patients to diagnosis-related groups (DRG); and consulting with physicians or others, or clarifying codes or diagnoses at coding team meetings, regarding conflicting, missing, or ambiguous information; second, registration and indexes and retrieval — planning, developing, maintaining, or operating various health record indexes or storage and retrieval systems to collect, classify, store, or analyze information; retrieving patient records for physicians, technicians, or other medical personnel; and maintaining registry data such as tumor registries; third, statistics and reporting — compiling medical and census data to produce statistical reports on diseases treated, surgeries performed, or bed occupancy, and compiling statistical reports, narrative reports, or graphic presentations for hospital staff, researchers, or other users; fourth, privacy and security and compliance — protecting the security of medical records to ensure confidentiality, monitoring changes in legislation and accreditation standards that affect the security or privacy of computerized healthcare systems, and promoting and facilitating activities to foster awareness of medical information privacy or security; fifth, systems and databases and training — applying knowledge of healthcare and information systems to assist in the design, development, and continued modification and analysis of computerized healthcare systems, designing databases that support healthcare applications and ensuring security, performance, and reliability, evaluating and recommending system upgrades or improvements, and developing in-service education materials and training medical records staff; sixth, management and collaboration — managing a department or supervising clerical staff and directing or controlling the activities of medical records department staff, and collaborating with clinical, management, and coding teams to resolve coding and data problems. Work cycle links: medical records and coding—registration and indexes and retrieval—statistics and reporting—privacy and security and compliance—systems and databases and training—management and collaboration and review. This page does not conflate this occupation with adjacent ones such as clinical data managers, clinical research coordinators, health informatics specialists, medical records specialists (medical records and health information technicians), document management specialists, medical and health services managers, patient representatives, or computer systems analysts, nor does it expand medical records and health information duties to the point of replacing clinical diagnosis, treatment, medication, or medical decisions.

Compliance and boundaries | Matters involving clinical judgment, diagnosis and treatment and medication, medical advice, or external disclosure must be carried out in accordance with institutional and legal and compliance requirements; the handling and disclosure of patient health information or protected health information must be confirmed by a position or institution with the corresponding authorization and compliance requirements.

Recording and collaboration note | Starting from medical records, classification standards, and information system requirements, first verify medical record completeness and the coding basis, classification and terminology standards and mapping, system interfaces and retrieval and performance, and privacy and security and minimum necessary requirements, and then carry out coding, registration, and statistics; coding and abstraction must follow standards and be reviewable; registration, index, and retrieval records must be traceable; statistical and reporting definitions must be defined in advance and documented; original records and revisions must leave an audit trail and must not be altered after the fact; patient health information or protected health information must be managed in accordance with privacy and compliance requirements and the minimum necessary principle; matters involving clinical judgment, medical advice, or external disclosure must be confirmed by a position or institution with the corresponding qualifications; and important coding, statistical, and record entries must be able to withstand review by superiors and by compliance and information security.

Mainland China scope and gaps | In mainland China, there are positions in the fields of medical record management, medical information, health statistics, hospital information, health records, and medical registration that are similar to Health Information Technologists and Medical Registrars (such as medical record administrators, medical record coders, medical information and health statistics personnel, hospital information department data and registration positions, and health records and medical data governance personnel); their work, qualifications, standards, and records are governed by the Basic Medical and Health Promotion Law of the People's Republic of China, the Cybersecurity Law of the People's Republic of China, the Data Security Law of the People's Republic of China, and the Personal Information Protection Law of the People's Republic of China, as well as regulations on medical record management, electronic medical records, and network and data security in medical institutions: the construction and operation of medical records and medical information systems must follow standards and specifications; matters involving diagnosis, treatment, and medication must be carried out by institutions and personnel with the corresponding qualifications; and patient health information and personal health information must be protected in accordance with the law and handled under the minimum necessary principle. However, this round did not obtain a national occupational wage distribution precisely corresponding to U.S. O*NET 29-9021.00 (Health Information Technologists and Medical Registrars): the National Bureau of Statistics publishes average wages of urban unit employees by industry category, which is an industry scope that does not distinguish occupations and does not list this occupation separately. Under the evidence policy, this page only registers the statistical scope and the visible gaps (marked "Evidence insufficient:") and does not use industry averages, job posting offers, or cross-jurisdiction extrapolation from U.S. wages for starting salaries, medians, or personal income; the two sets of scope, mainland China and the United States, differ in legal environment and statistical period, and are not combined or converted.

Ethics and privacy note | Organize work according to patient information privacy and security and data protection requirements: medical records and coding and registration and statistical materials must be consistent with current standards and specifications and must state their sources and limitations, and must not replace clinical diagnosis, treatment and medication, or medical advice; data involving patients and users must follow the principles of minimum necessary, purpose limitation, and de-identification; patient health information or protected health information must be accessed, stored, and shared in accordance with institutional and legal requirements; access control, auditing, and backup must be carried out in accordance with information security requirements; coding and registration and system changes and releases must undergo the necessary review and verification; and upon finding that a medical record is unclear or the coding basis is insufficient or standards do not match, that a system deviates from compliance requirements, that a security or privacy risk arises, or that clinical advice is involved or authorization is exceeded, work must pause immediately and be reported and reviewed according to policy. The content on this page does not constitute any medical, diagnostic, treatment, medication, legal, or compliance advice.

Standards and quality boundaries | This page involves three types of requirements: first, professional and quality, meaning coding, abstraction, registration, and statistics must be carried out on the basis of medical records and current classification standards and specifications, with coding, registration, statistics, and system operation records kept; second, ethics and privacy and security, meaning medical records and data must follow the minimum necessary, purpose limitation, access control, and auditing principles, and patient health information or protected health information must be managed in accordance with institutional and legal requirements, and clinical judgment or diagnosis and medication advice must not be provided beyond boundaries; third, records and information, meaning coding, registration, index, retrieval, statistical, and system operation records must be truthful, complete, and traceable, and materials that are controlled or involve patient health information and externally disclosed information must be managed according to approval and the minimum necessary principle. This page provides general guidance only and does not constitute medical, diagnostic, treatment, medication, legal, or compliance advice.

Recording and collaboration | Record, in accordance with institutional medical record, informatization, information security, and data management policies, the patients and roles and permissions, medical records and coding basis and classification standards, registration and indexes and retrieval, statistical definitions and sources, exceptions and omissions and handling, review and changes and releases, and original records and revision audit trails, and complete them using the prescribed templates and time limits; upon finding that a medical record is unclear or the coding basis is insufficient or standards do not match, that a system deviates from compliance requirements, that a security or privacy risk arises, or that records and the actual situation are inconsistent, pause immediately, report according to authorization, and ask compliance and information security and clinical positions to review, and do not modify records without authorization or make retrospective entries.

Boundary conclusion | This page corresponds to O*NET 29-9021.00 (Health Information Technologists and Medical Registrars), and the core difference from adjacent positions lies in "subject matter, output, and authorization level": this occupation takes the operation and support of medical records, coding, registration, statistics, and health information systems as its subject matter, and its output is coding, registration, retrieval, statistical, and system operation records completed according to medical records, classification standards, and information system requirements; Medical Records Specialists (medical records and health information technicians, 29-2072.00) take the operation and support of medical records and health information technology as their subject matter; Document Management Specialists (15-1299.03) take document and records management as their subject matter; Health Informatics Specialists (15-1211.01) take the design and implementation of health information systems as their subject matter; Clinical Data Managers (15-2051.02) take clinical research data management as their subject matter; Clinical Research Coordinators (11-9121.01) take clinical research project coordination as their subject matter; Computer Systems Analysts (15-1211.00) take general information system analysis and design as their subject matter; Medical and Health Services Managers (11-9111.00) take medical service operations management as their subject matter; and Patient Representatives (29-2099.08) take patient communication and rights assistance as their subject matter. Subject matter, output, and authorization level all differ, and the authority for clinical judgment, medical advice, system design, and disclosure cannot be carried over across positions.

Core concept of adjacent positions | Positions in the same group and adjacent positions mostly aim to "process medical records, data, documents, systems, research, or services to the prescribed state within standards, compliance, and authorization boundaries and leave an audit trail," and they differ in subject matter, output, and authorization level: some take medical records and coding and registration and statistics as their subject matter, while others take medical records and health information technology support, document management, health information system design, clinical research data, research coordination, general systems analysis, medical operations, or patient assistance as theirs.

Core purpose of this occupation | Taking medical records, classification standards, information systems, and data as its subject matter, complete the work within standards, compliance, and authorization: medical records and coding, registration and indexes and retrieval, statistics and reporting, privacy and security and compliance, systems and databases and training, and management and collaboration and review, so that medical records and coding are accurate, registration and statistics and retrieval are traceable, patient information privacy and security are controlled, and responsibility boundaries can be explained.

Main subject matter and basis of adjacent positions | Medical Records Specialists rely on medical records and medical record and health information management standards; Document Management Specialists rely on document and records management and information governance standards; Health Informatics Specialists rely on health information system and data standards and information security standards; Clinical Data Managers rely on clinical research data management and quality standards; Clinical Research Coordinators rely on clinical research standards and regulations; Computer Systems Analysts rely on general information system analysis and software engineering methods; Medical and Health Services Managers rely on medical service operations and management standards; and Patient Representatives rely on patient service and rights assistance standards.

Main subject matter and basis of this occupation | The subject matter is medical record completeness and coding basis, classification and terminology standards and mapping, registration and indexes and retrieval, statistical definitions and sources, privacy and security and access control, and systems and databases and training, based on medical record and health information management standards, medical information privacy and security and data protection standards, and institutional medical record and data policies.

Occupational profile | The Health Information Technologists and Medical Registrars on this page is the exact occupation O*NET 29-9021.00 (Health Information Technologists and Medical Registrars), which in medical institutions and in medical records, health information, health data, and medical insurance settings carries out medical records, coding, registration, statistics, and health information system operation and support work: using standard classification systems to identify, compile, abstract, and code patient data, assigning patients to diagnosis-related groups (DRG), planning and maintaining health record indexes and storage and retrieval systems, compiling statistical reports and graphic presentations, protecting the security of medical records and monitoring changes in legislation and accreditation standards related to information security and privacy, assisting in the design and development and modification of healthcare systems and databases and developing in-service education materials and training personnel, and managing a department or supervising clerical staff. Common job titles include Medical Records Analyst and Medical Records Director. On the 29-9021.00 page, O*NET shows that the main industry for this occupation in the United States is healthcare and social assistance. The interest code is CIS (Conventional—Investigative—Social), with occupational interest type scores of Conventional (83), Investigative (70), and Social (47); the highest work style influence scores are Attention to Detail (92), Dependability (88), Integrity (84), and Cautiousness (76). O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Three (medium preparation needed, SVP 6.0 to less than 7.0); the education section of that page does not show a percentage distribution, and this page does not fill it in. This page is a "subset profile" and does not provide work context percentages or task importance scores, and this page marks the corresponding dimensions with "Evidence insufficient:". Core processes of adjacent positions | Medical Records Specialists focus on medical record organization and coding and health information technology support; Document Management Specialists focus on the collection, classification, archiving, and retrieval of documents and records; Health Informatics Specialists focus on translating requirements and designing and implementing systems; Clinical Data Managers focus on clinical research data collection, cleaning, and quality control; Clinical Research Coordinators focus on research project coordination and subject management and compliance; Computer Systems Analysts focus on general business requirements analysis and system design; Medical and Health Services Managers focus on service operations and workforce and budget management; and Patient Representatives focus on patient communication and rights assistance.

Core processes of this occupation | Medical records and coding, registration and indexes and retrieval, statistics and reporting, privacy and security and compliance, systems and databases and training, and management and collaboration and review; every step must leave an audit trail in accordance with medical record and information security and data policies and must be reviewable by superiors and by compliance and clinical staff.

Main outputs of adjacent positions | Medical Records Specialists produce medical records and coding and health information technology support records; Document Management Specialists produce document and records management and retrieval records; Health Informatics Specialists produce system design and configuration and monitoring records; Clinical Data Managers produce clinical research data and quality records; Clinical Research Coordinators produce research project coordination and compliance records; Computer Systems Analysts produce business requirements and system design documents; Medical and Health Services Managers produce operations and budget and workforce documents; and Patient Representatives produce patient communication and assistance records.

Main outputs of this occupation | Coding, abstraction, and grouping records of patient data completed according to medical records and classification standards; health record index and storage and retrieval and registration records; statistical reports and narrative reports and graphic presentations; privacy and security and confidentiality and awareness activity records; database and system support and upgrade recommendations and in-service training records; department management and process and review records; and traceable compliance and data protection and validation records.

Responsibility holder for adjacent positions | Responsibility for positions in the same group and adjacent positions is usually defined by the employing institution together with professional and compliance and regulatory standards, and the objects of responsibility are mostly clinical and business users and patient information and data accuracy and institutional compliance.

This occupation is responsible for the coding, abstraction, registration, index, retrieval, statistical, and system operation records that the individual performs and signs, and for the work and conclusions completed according to medical records, classification standards, and information security and data policies; matters involving clinical judgment and diagnosis and treatment and medication, medical advice, system design and external disclosure, and the handling and disclosure of patient health information are decided according to policy by a position or institution with the corresponding qualifications, and this occupation does not replace those decisions.

Authority and approval for adjacent positions | The authority of positions in the same group and adjacent positions comes from institutional authorization together with professional and compliance and regulatory standards, and generally does not include the authority to decide on their own conclusions and signatures and releases that exceed their own authorization or scope; matters involving clinical decisions and major disclosures and design decisions should be referred to the corresponding position or institution.

Authority and approval for this occupation | Routine coding, registration, retrieval, statistics, system operations, and training must be carried out within standards and the scope of institutional authorization; matters involving clinical judgment, medical advice, external disclosure, and the handling and disclosure of patient health information must be carried out according to qualifications and approval; changes to coding rules and statistical definitions and system releases must obtain approval from the corresponding position or institution according to policy, or be referred onward, and must not be judged or released beyond authority.

Boundaries of conclusions for adjacent positions | Conclusions of positions in the same group and adjacent positions are mostly limited to the level of their own project and their own duties, and generally do not constitute a determination of clinical outcomes or medical diagnosis or legal liability or the accuracy of data results; the application of conclusions that cross specialties or involve clinical matters and major disclosures has its own scope limits.

Boundaries of conclusions for this occupation | Coding, registration, and statistical conclusions state only verifiable medical records and coding basis and classification standards and data and statistical definition records, and distinguish measured facts from judgment inferences and items pending verification; unauthorized judgments and commitments must not be made on matters beyond one's own authorization (clinical judgment, medical advice, system design and external disclosure, handling and disclosure of patient health information); when a medical record is unclear or the coding basis is insufficient or standards do not match, when a system deviates from compliance requirements, when there is a security or privacy risk, or when records and the actual situation are inconsistent, work must pause and be escalated or referred onward, and conclusions must also be able to withstand review by superiors and by compliance and information security and clinical and regulatory inspection.

This page lists verification directions only and does not constitute a formal conditions checklist for any institution or position. Special note: in the United States, this occupation falls under O*NET Job Zone Three (medium preparation needed, SVP 6.0 to less than 7.0); in mainland China, positions involving medical records and medical information and health statistics often have requirements for professional and continuing education and medical record coding qualifications, so be sure to confirm the position's specific requirements for education and training and certification and continuing education and the handling of patient health information and position authorization.

Notes on verification points | Positions with similar titles differ greatly in duties and authorization: some focus on medical records and coding and grouping, some on registration and indexes and retrieval and statistics, some on medical records and health information technology support, some on medical data governance and quality, and some on medical insurance and compliance auditing; different institutions and jurisdictions also differ in the authorization for clinical advice, data and privacy, coding rules, and external disclosure.

01 Actual duties and authorization boundaries of the position | Verify whether the role genuinely involves independent coding, abstraction, registration, statistics, and retrieval work, or is mainly medical record organization and data entry and assistance; verify the coding and classification and statistical tools and systems and retrieval permissions that may be used, the approval requirements for accessing and handling and disclosing patient health information and protected health information, the authority to determine coding rules and statistical definitions, and the collaboration and reporting paths with compliance and information security and clinical and statistical functions.

Notes on verification points | This occupation frequently communicates and collaborates with clinical and business users and coding and statistical and management departments, and usually requires training and continuing education related to medical records or medical information or health information or health data.

02 Ethics and privacy and security requirements | Verify whether the institution requires and provides: minimum necessary and purpose limitation and de-identification requirements; requirements for accessing and storing and sharing and disclosing patient health information or protected health information; access control and auditing and encryption and backup requirements; coding and classification standards and validation and review requirements; registration and indexes and statistical definitions and release review requirements; data security incident and gap and reporting requirements; personal information protection and cybersecurity and data security requirements; and compliance and information security and clinical review paths. The content on this page does not constitute any medical, diagnostic, treatment, medication, legal, or compliance advice.

Notes on verification points | U.S. O*NET places 29-9021.00 (Health Information Technologists and Medical Registrars) in Job Zone Three (medium preparation needed), with an SVP range of 6.0 to less than 7.0; the education section of that page does not show a percentage distribution, and this page does not fill it in; the interest code is CIS (Conventional—Investigative—Social). This description does not replace the employer's and the competent authority's requirements for education and training and certification and continuing education and qualifications, and does not constitute any hiring condition.

03 Education and training and qualification requirements | Verify whether a degree and training related to medical records or medical information or health information or health data is required, whether coding and classification and statistics and information system skills are required, whether certifications related to medical records and coding or health information are required (the O*NET certification directory lists several medical record and health information certifications, such as the American Health Information Management Association's Registered Health Information Administrator and Registered Health Information Technician and Certified Coding Specialist and Certified Health Data Analyst, and the National Cancer Registrars Association's Certified Tumor Registrar), whether continuing education is required to maintain certification, and the institution's internal conditions for obtaining the right to independently sign coding and statistical and release records.

Notes on verification points | This occupation focuses on medical records and coding and registration and statistics and system operations, and the work tends to concentrate around coding and statistical and compliance and inspection checkpoints, which may lead to concentrated overtime; compensation usually consists of base salary plus coding and certification allowances and bonuses, and working hours and projects and allowances and performance criteria must be confirmed in writing. O*NET 29-9021.00 is a subset profile and does not provide work context percentages; this page does not fill them in with values from adjacent occupations.

04 Compensation and working hours and employment contract scope | Verify the composition of the offered compensation (base salary, coding and certification and on-call allowances, overtime and travel subsidies, bonuses, training and continuing education and certification maintenance arrangements), working hours and coding and statistical and inspection checkpoint arrangements, contract term and project type, probation period and performance criteria (coding accuracy and compliance and data and security and collaboration indicators), and whether patient health information and protected health information and trade secrets and personal information protection and position responsibility and insurance arrangements are involved.

Notes on verification points | The interface relationships with compliance and information security and clinical and statistical functions determine the boundaries of medical records and data and responsibility and disclosure, and must be clarified in advance.

05 Interface authority with compliance and information security and clinical and statistical functions | Verify the access paths to medical records and data and systems, the application and use and approval arrangements for coding and classification and statistical tools and retrieval permissions, the reporting and handling and escalation paths for unclear medical records or insufficient coding basis or non-conforming standards or security or privacy risks, the approval for clinical advice and the handling of patient health information and external disclosure and statistical release, and cross-department and cross-institution handover and division of responsibility.

Notes on verification points | The traceability and audit trail requirements for medical records and coding and registration and index and retrieval and statistical records determine compliance and the definition of responsibility, and the specifications for templates and time limits and modification and archiving and permissions and retention periods must be clarified in advance (materials involving patient health information or protected health information must also be managed according to privacy and minimum necessary requirements).

paragraphs: Conclusion | The core difference between this page (O*NET 29-9021.00 Health Information Technologists and Medical Registrars) and adjacent positions lies in "subject matter, output, and authorization level": this occupation takes the operation and support of medical records, coding, registration, statistics, and health information systems as its subject matter, and its output is coding, registration, retrieval, statistical, and system operation records completed according to medical records, classification standards, and information system requirements; Medical Records Specialists (medical records and health information technicians, 29-2072.00) take the operation and support of medical records and health information technology as their subject matter; Document Management Specialists (15-1299.03) take document and records management as their subject matter; Health Informatics Specialists (15-1211.01) take the design and implementation of health information systems as their subject matter; Clinical Data Managers (15-2051.02) take clinical research data management as their subject matter; and Medical and Health Services Managers (11-9111.00) take medical service operations management as their subject matter. Subject matter, output, and authorization level all differ, and the authority for clinical judgment, medical advice, system design, and disclosure cannot be carried over across positions.

Evidence note | The comparison subjects in the table below come from the O*NET occupational classification and public materials, and are intended to help distinguish the work content of adjacent occupations and choose a fit; they do not constitute qualification, hiring, or compensation conclusions, nor do they constitute medical, diagnostic, treatment, medication, legal, or compliance advice. The wages and employment of each occupation must be verified separately under its own SOC scope; this table does not make numerical comparisons, nor does it treat one occupation's wages as a proxy for another's; qualification and compliance and data requirements must be verified according to each jurisdiction and institution. The U.S. wage and employment on this page follow this occupation's (29-9021.00) own scope as presented by O*NET on the 29-9021.00 page (that page does not mark them as taken from a parent occupation and shows projected growth of 7% or higher), and values from adjacent occupations are not borrowed.

Preface | The following comparison is organized in four columns: "career direction—core work and output—key differences—who it suits better." Medical records, coding, registration and statistics, documents, and information systems are often connected within the same medical institution or health information department, but connection does not mean they are interchangeable; when choosing across directions, you should relearn that direction's subject matter and standards and data and authorization and responsibility boundaries.

Key differences: this occupation takes the operation and support of medical records, coding, registration, statistics, and health information systems as its subject matter, and, drawing on medical record and health information knowledge, completes coding and registration and statistics and system operations within compliance and authorization and produces records and reports, being responsible for data accuracy and privacy and records; the other positions center respectively on medical records and health information technology support, document and records management, health information system design, clinical research data management, or medical service operations management, and each usually has more specialized standards and authorization and subject matter, and none bears primary responsibility for medical records and coding and registration and statistics (though they must collaborate with this occupation and clearly define boundaries).

Better suited to people who are willing to process medical records and coding and registration and statistics and retrieval item by item according to standards and specifications, can communicate with clinical and management departments, and are willing to take responsibility for data accuracy and patient information privacy.

Core work and output: use standard classification systems to identify and compile and abstract and code patient data and assign patients to diagnosis-related groups, plan and maintain health record indexes and storage and retrieval systems and retrieve medical records for medical personnel, compile medical and census data and produce statistical reports and graphic presentations, protect the security of medical records and monitor changes in legislation and accreditation standards related to information security and privacy, assist in the design and development and modification of healthcare systems and databases and develop in-service education materials and train personnel, and manage a department or supervise clerical staff; the output is coding, registration, retrieval, statistical, and system operation records completed according to medical records, classification standards, and information system requirements (O*NET/SOC 29-9021.00).
This occupation: Health Information Technologists and Medical Registrars (O*NET/SOC 29-9021.00, Health Information Technologists and Medical Registrars)

Key differences: Medical Records Specialists take the operation and support of medical records and health information technology as their subject matter, and their output is medical records and coding and health information technology support records; in addition to medical records and coding, this occupation also handles registration and indexes and retrieval and statistics and health information system operation and support, and its output is registration and retrieval and statistical and system operation records; the two are highly adjacent, but this occupation places more emphasis on registration and statistics and system support (collaboration with Medical Records Specialists is needed to keep data consistent).

Better suited to people who are willing to work on medical record organization and coding and health information technology support; this occupation leans more toward the combined responsibilities of coding and registration and retrieval and statistics and system support.

Core work and output: organize medical records and perform coding and health information technology support according to medical records and medical record and health information management standards and keep records; the output is medical records and coding and health information technology support records.
Medical Records Specialists (29-2072.00)

Key differences: Document Management Specialists take the collection and classification and archiving and retrieval and information governance of documents and records as their subject matter, and their output is document and records management and retrieval records; this occupation takes medical records and coding and registration and statistics and health information systems as its subject matter, and its output is coding and registration and retrieval and statistical records, and generally does not bear primary responsibility for the institution's general document and records governance (though collaboration with Document Management Specialists is needed to keep record practices consistent).

Better suited to people who are willing to work on general document and records management and information governance; this occupation leans more toward the professional operations of medical records and coding and registration and statistics and health information systems.

Core work and output: collect and classify and archive and retrieve documents and records according to document and information governance standards and maintain versions and permissions; the output is document and records management and retrieval records.
Document Management Specialists (15-1299.03)

Key differences: Health Informatics Specialists take the translation of clinical and business requirements and the design and implementation of health information systems as their subject matter, and their output is system design and configuration and monitoring records; this occupation takes medical records and coding and registration and statistics and system operations as its subject matter, and its output is coding and registration and retrieval and statistical records, and generally does not bear primary responsibility for the design and implementation of health information systems (though collaboration with Health Informatics Specialists is needed to align system and data standards).

Better suited to people who are willing to work on translating clinical requirements and system design and implementation; this occupation leans more toward medical records and coding and registration and statistics and system operation support.

Core work and output: translate clinical and business requirements into system solutions and design and configure and test and monitor information systems; the output is system design and configuration and monitoring records.
Health Informatics Specialists (15-1211.01)

Key differences: Clinical Data Managers take clinical research data management and quality control as their subject matter, and their output is clinical research data and quality records; this occupation takes medical records and coding and registration and statistics as its subject matter, and its output is coding and registration and retrieval and statistical records, and generally does not bear primary responsibility for clinical research data management (though collaboration with Clinical Data Managers is needed to keep data standards consistent).

Better suited to people who are willing to work on clinical research data collection and cleaning and quality control and statistical collaboration; this occupation leans more toward medical records and coding and registration and statistics and system operations.

Core work and output: collect and clean and validate research data according to clinical research data management and quality standards and support statistics and reporting; the output is clinical research data and quality records.
Clinical Data Managers (15-2051.02)

Key differences: Medical and Health Services Managers take medical service operations and workforce and budget management as their subject matter, and their output is operations and budget and workforce documents; this occupation takes medical records and coding and registration and statistics as its subject matter, and its output is coding and registration and retrieval and statistical records, and generally does not bear primary responsibility for department operations and workforce and budget management (though collaboration with Medical and Health Services Managers is needed to align processes and resources).

Better suited to people who are willing to work on medical service operations and workforce and budget management; this occupation leans more toward medical records and coding and registration and statistics and system operation support.

Core work and output: develop operations and workforce and budget plans according to medical service operations and management standards and coordinate cross-departmental implementation; the output is operations and budget and workforce documents.
Medical and Health Services Managers (11-9111.00)

Transition | This page places adjacent positions side by side by "subject matter, output, and authorization level" to help you judge which kind of medical record or coding or registration and statistics or health information system or document or research data or medical operations position you want to invest in long term. What kind of personality is better suited to being a Health Information Technologist and Medical Registrar? This occupation values attentiveness and adherence to standards, a sense of responsibility for patient information and confidentiality, communication and collaboration skills, and stability under statistical and inspection pressure, rather than any particular personality type; the O*NET interest code is CIS (Conventional—Investigative—Social), and among the work style influences Attention to Detail (92), Dependability (88), and Integrity (84) rank highest, which can serve as a starting point for exploration.

Are introverts suited to this occupation? Yes. This occupation involves a great deal of desk work on coding and data and registration and statistics, and it also requires communicating with the coding team and medical personnel and management departments (work style influence "Collaboration (64)").

Introversion and extraversion are not a validated fit threshold here; you can observe how the person explains health information, listens to patients' and users' needs, and confirms understanding. No occupational-level comparative validity research was obtained.

Which MBTI type is most suitable for this occupation? No type has been proven most suitable. The MBTI is not an occupational qualification or ability assessment tool, and occupational fit depends mainly on skills and compliance adherence and attentiveness.

Which Holland interest type is more suitable for this occupation? The O*NET interest code is CIS: Conventional (executing according to standards and specifications and records), Investigative (medical records and data and statistical research), and Social (communicating and collaborating with medical personnel and the coding team); it can be used to explore task preferences, not to predict performance.
This page does not provide validation research on how personality or interests affect work performance in this occupation, and no individual performance conclusions are drawn from questionnaires.

Can someone who is not good at math do this occupation? Basic data and statistics and classification and logical interpretation abilities are needed; a quantitative foundation can be filled in through training and tool support, but a complete inability to adapt to data and coding would be clearly limiting.

Does this occupation require high emotional intelligence? It requires emotional stability and patience and collaboration skills, but no specific assessment scores; statistical and inspection and security incident pressure requires self-regulation and communicating and reporting according to procedure.

Can the Enneagram be used to judge whether I am suited? No. The Enneagram is a self-exploration tool and does not constitute a conclusion about occupational ability or fit; judging fit should look at whether you can complete coding and registration and retrieval and statistics work under standards and compliance and authorization requirements.

The editors recommend using approved de-identified materials to verify patients and users, evidence, indicators, and methods; this is an exploration recommendation and does not prove greater predictive accuracy than a questionnaire. Access to real projects and data is carried out according to authorization.

items.title: Education, training, and qualifications: which are the real thresholds for this occupation?

paragraphs: Qualification boundary one | Job requirements, education, proof of training, medical record and coding or health information-related certification and continuing education, health and occupational health examinations, institutional and position authorization, and statistical release and external disclosure authority are different states: meeting hiring requirements does not equal obtaining the authority to independently release statistics or issue statistical conclusions or compliance advice. entries.answer: The Health Information Technologists and Medical Registrars on this page is the exact occupation O*NET 29-9021.00 (Health Information Technologists and Medical Registrars): apply knowledge of healthcare and information systems to assist in the design, development, and continued modification and analysis of computerized healthcare systems; abstract, collect, and analyze treatment and followup information of patients; may educate staff and assist in problem solving to promote the implementation of the healthcare information system; may design, develop, test, and implement databases with complete history, diagnosis, treatment, and health status to help monitor diseases. Core tasks include using standard classification systems to identify and compile and abstract and code patient data and assign patients to diagnosis-related groups (DRG), protecting the security of medical records to ensure confidentiality, monitoring changes in legislation and accreditation standards that affect the security or privacy of information systems, planning and maintaining health record indexes and storage and retrieval systems, compiling statistical reports and graphic presentations, designing databases that support healthcare applications, and training medical records staff. Common job titles include Medical Records Analyst and Medical Records Director; on the 29-9021.00 page, O*NET shows that the main industry for this occupation in the United States is healthcare and social assistance. What is described on this page is the U.S. occupational classification scope, and wages and employment follow this occupation's (29-9021.00) own scope; this page is a subset profile and does not provide work context percentages or task importance scores, and this page does not fill them in; the content on this page does not constitute any medical, diagnostic, treatment, medication, legal, or compliance advice.

entries.answer: The core differences lie in subject matter, output, and authorization level: this occupation takes the operation and support of medical records, coding, registration, statistics, and health information systems as its subject matter, and its output is coding, registration, retrieval, statistical, and system operation records completed according to medical records, classification standards, and information system requirements; Medical Records Specialists (medical records and health information technicians, 29-2072.00) take the operation and support of medical records and health information technology as their subject matter; Document Management Specialists (15-1299.03) take document and records management as their subject matter; Health Informatics Specialists (15-1211.01) take the design and implementation of health information systems as their subject matter; Clinical Data Managers (15-2051.02) take clinical research data management as their subject matter; Clinical Research Coordinators (11-9121.01) take clinical research project coordination as their subject matter; Computer Systems Analysts (15-1211.00) take general information system analysis and design as their subject matter; Medical and Health Services Managers (11-9111.00) take medical service operations management as their subject matter; and Patient Representatives (29-2099.08) take patient communication and rights assistance as their subject matter. Subject matter and work and authorization level all differ, and the authority for clinical judgment and medical advice and system design and disclosure cannot be carried over across positions.

subject.name: Health Information Technologists and Medical Registrars
subject.summary: The Health Information Technologists and Medical Registrars corresponds to the exact occupation O*NET/SOC 29-9021.00 "Health Information Technologists and Medical Registrars": apply knowledge of healthcare and information systems to assist in the design, development, and continued modification and analysis of computerized healthcare systems; abstract, collect, and analyze treatment and followup information of patients; may educate staff and assist in problem solving to promote the implementation of the healthcare information system; may design, develop, test, and implement databases with complete history, diagnosis, treatment, and health status to help monitor diseases; core tasks include using standard classification systems to identify, compile, abstract, and code patient data and assigning patients to diagnosis-related groups, protecting the security of medical records to ensure confidentiality, monitoring changes in legislation and accreditation standards that affect the security or privacy of information systems, planning and maintaining health record indexes and storage and retrieval systems, compiling statistical reports and graphic presentations, and designing databases that support healthcare applications and training medical records staff; common job titles include Medical Records Analyst and Medical Records Director. Official scope text: Apply knowledge of healthcare and information systems to assist in the design, development, and continued modification and analysis of computerized healthcare systems. Abstract, collect, and analyze treatment and followup information of patients. May educate staff and assist in problem solving to promote the implementation of the healthcare information system. May design, develop, test, and implement databases with complete history, diagnosis, treatment, and health status to help monitor diseases. Scope note: the U.S. wage and employment and industry data presented by O*NET on the 29-9021.00 page are not marked as taken from a parent occupation, so this page labels them faithfully according to this occupation's own scope (29-9021.00); this occupation is projected to grow 7% or higher over 2024—2034 and is marked Bright Outlook, and O*NET places it in Job Zone Three (medium preparation needed, SVP 6.0 to less than 7.0); this page is a "subset profile" and does not provide educational attainment distribution, work context percentages, or task importance scores, and this page marks them with "Evidence insufficient:" rather than filling them in. The content on this page does not constitute medical, diagnostic, treatment, medication, legal, or compliance advice.
